messages:
sara (support): escalating: Acme customer reporting spikes of 504s and 5xxs from the hosted inference endpoint (model: redwood-13b-v1). They see ~15% failure rate during peak minutes. Customer says errors started ~2026-03-14 17:12 UTC, repeated every ~10–15 minutes. Sample request-ids: r-8a1f2e, r-8a1f9b, r-8a20c3. They included logs showing gateway timeout and backend 502s. Marking P1 due to revenue impact and SLA. cc @alex (oncall) and @tomas (runtime).

sara (support): repro steps provided by customer:
1) POST /v1/generate with long prompt (~1.6k tokens) and stream disabled
2) concurrency of 30 clients hitting same model/route
3) period of sustained traffic for ~3 minutes
They also said retry/backoff doesn't help for tail requests — immediate retries hit same tail.

alex (oncall): seeing alerts now in paging — multiple "request_queue_depth" spikes and "batcher_backlog" > 1000 around the same timestamps. Throttles kicking in: gateway returning 502/504 after internal timeout. I'm on it. Sharing dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/d/queues/hosted

deploy-bot: automated message: high request latency spike detected for model=redwood-13b-v1 region=us-west-2 window=5m. active_batchers=12 backlog=1187 queue_depth_limit=1024

tomas (runtime): looking at runtime logs for those request-ids. I see continuous-batching backlog growth:
```
[17:12:02] batcher.c: enqueue request r-8a1f2e queue_pos=960 backlog=960
[17:12:03] batcher.c: enqueue request r-8a1f9b queue_pos=972 backlog=972
[17:12:05] batcher.c: backlog=1187 queue_depth_limit=1024 -> triggering early_reject
[17:12:05] runtime: returning 502 to gateway for request r-8a1f2e reason=queue_overflow
```
Looks like the queue_depth_limit is being hit and we have early rejects. Continuous batching waits for batch timeout to try to aggregate, but when backlog >> depth limit we reject. The long prompts increase per-request GPU time so queue doesn't drain.

tomas (runtime): quick mitigation ideas:
- temporarily raise queue_depth_limit to 4096 for hosted pool (hotfix) and spin up 4 extra batchers to increase throughput
- reduce batch_max_wait_ms from 25ms to 10ms to lower tail latency for small batches (tradeoff: slightly fewer tokens-per-batch)
- enable per-tenant concurrency cap for Acme as a throttle while we stabilize

anya (infra): raising queue_depth_limit has memory/CPU implications on leader process. If we jump to 4096, we need to ensure batcher memory handles KV cache pressure. I'd prefer a gradual bump and enabling short-term route-fallback to a smaller model like redwood-7b-8k for that tenant. Also we can enable auto-burst workers in Dedicated, but for Hosted we need canary first. I'll run a canary to 10% traffic after we change defaults.

alex (oncall): immediate plan:
- sara to send remediation to customer: ask to reduce client concurrency to <=10 and add exponential backoff (retry-after recommended). include the temporary mitigation (route fallback) if they accept degraded model.
- tomas to prepare hotfix PR to bump queue_depth_limit and batch_max_wait_ms in hosted config
- anya to run canary + monitor memory and KV hit rates
- I'll monitor errors and hold page until stable
ETA 30m for hotfix canary

sara (support): message to Acme drafted:
"Hi — we’re investigating intermittent 502/504s. Short-term action: please reduce concurrency to <=10 and implement exponential backoff (jitter). We can enable a fallback route to a smaller model if you want a quick mitigation with slightly different outputs. We’ll update you with a rollback plan and timeline. —Sara"

customer-acme (external): thanks, will throttle to 8 clients and test. we need to keep throughput though, can we get an ETA on fix? Our launch window is tomorrow.

tomas (runtime): making a hotfix PR now. config diff (hosted default):
```
- queue_depth_limit: 1024
- batch_max_wait_ms: 25
+ queue_depth_limit: 2048  # initial bump
+ batch_max_wait_ms: 12
```
I'll start with 2048 not 4096 for canary. If stable, we can raise further. Also adding a soft per-tenant limit for Acme: tenant_max_concurrency: 12

tomas (runtime): repro note for engineering: to reproduce locally use the stress script:
```
./tools/stress_requests --model redwood-13b-v1 --concurrency 30 --prompt-size 1600 --duration 180
```
This reliably pushes backlog in our staging pool when run from multiple clients.

anya (infra): canary started (canary_id c-7723) routing 5% of traffic to updated config in us-west-2. Observing memory and batcher queues. Setting alert if batcher_backlog > 800.

deploy-bot: canary event: c-7723 started for config: hosted/queue-tuning-1801234567

alex (oncall): monitoring metrics — backlog dropped from 1187 to 420 in canary nodes within 2m. Errors on canary nodes reduced. Non-canary still seeing spikes. Good sign.

sara (support): customer confirmed reduced concurrency; they reported immediate drop in 5xx for their traffic to near 0% after throttling. They want the final fix applied to prod pool asap.

tomas (runtime): after 12m of canary and stable metrics, proposing rollout 50% -> 100% in 10m increments. Also adding a short-term automated fallback policy: when queue_depth > 1500, route 30% of new tenant requests to redwood-7b-8k. This should prevent whole-pool saturation.

anya (infra): agree to rollout plan. will watch KV memory and set rollback threshold: if host memory free < 8% or swap used > 0% rollback immediately.

alex (oncall): proceed with staged rollout. I'll maintain pager watch. Noting next steps for postmortem: determine if the batching heuristic should account for prompt_length distribution and tenant imbalance. Also examine whether queue_depth_limit should be dynamic per model/hardware.

sara (support): I'll update the customer with the staged rollout plan and expected timeframe. Also recommended they implement jittered exponential backoff in SDK and added sample code snippet.

sara (support): sample backoff snippet:
```
for attempt in range(max_retries):
    try:
        call_api()
    except HTTPError as e:
        sleep(random.uniform(0, (2 ** attempt) * base))
```

customer-acme (external): confirmed reduced errors after we throttled on our side. appreciate the quick action. please keep us posted during rollout.

deploy-bot: rollout event: config hosted/queue-tuning-1801234567 at 50% -> backlog metrics stable

tomas (runtime): rollout to 100% completed. backlog metrics normalized across all pools; observed token throughput increase ~22% and tail p99 latency down from 1.2s to 0.6s for these workloads.

anya (infra): no memory or swap alarms during rollout. clearing canary watch.

alex (oncall): closing pager. assigning follow-ups:
- tomas: implement adaptive queue_depth based on prompt length distribution (ticket INF-582)
- infra: evaluate per-tenant throttling defaults and SDK guidance (ticket INF-583)
- support: send postmortem summary to Acme and record timeline (ticket CS-412)

sara (support): thanks team. I'll follow up on timing and paste the final timeline into the CS ticket. :thumbsup:

-- End of thread --
